items.title: Black Friday Streaming Deals: HBO Max, Disney+/Hulu Bundle, Apple TV Starting at $4.99/Month
items.summary:
The major streaming services have moved their Black Friday promotions early, with discounted annual and multi-month plans now live across HBO Max, the Disney+ and Hulu bundle, Apple TV, Paramount+ and Peacock. Consequence rounded up the offers, which run through Cyber Monday, November 30th. Several of them can also be activated as Prime Video add-ons rather than directly through the services themselves.

The steepest percentage cut belongs to the Disney+ and Hulu bundle, which drops to $4.99 a month with ads for a year, a 62% discount, or $14.99 a month ad-free, down 31%. HBO Max is offering 50% off its ad-supported tier for a year, bringing it to $5.49 a month, with the catalog covering series including The White Lotus, Euphoria and The Rehearsal alongside films such as Sinners and Wuthering Heights.

Apple TV is selling six months at $6.99 a month, a 53% reduction from its standard $14.99 rate, covering Severance, Slow Horses, Silo, Shrinking and For All Mankind. Paramount+ has the shortest window: two months of any tier at $2.99 a month, which amounts to nearly 80% off the $13.99 ad-free premium price and includes NFL, UFC and UEFA Champions League coverage.

Peacock's offer splits across two tiers. The ad-supported Select plan is 66% off for three months at $2.99 a month, or $29.99 for a first year, while the ad-supported Premium plan runs $8.99 a month for three months or $89.99 for the year. Select is the more limited of the two, restricted to programming that aired on NBC, including The Office and Law & Order.

All of the offers are time-limited and tied to commitment windows rather than open-ended rates, meaning the monthly prices revert once the promotional period ends. Pricing and availability remain subject to change through the Cyber Monday deadline.

items.title: Tidal Bans AI-Generated Music
items.summary:
Tidal said Tuesday that it will remove tracks it determines are entirely AI-generated from its catalog, beginning December 9. The decision makes Tidal the first music streaming platform to impose a full ban on AI-made music rather than labeling or demonetizing it.

Robert Andersen, who leads Tidal at parent company Block, laid out the reasoning in a thread on X. He wrote that 43% of tracks delivered to the service over the previous 90 days had been detected as AI-generated, adding, "Something more drastic needs to be done." According to Andersen, 96% of those AI tracks receive zero plays.

Variety reported that the purge will strip roughly 29 million tracks from Tidal's catalog, and that the service expects to reject between 80,000 and 85,000 submissions a day going forward. Andersen said the removals should be finished by the beginning of the year, and urged rival platforms to do the same: "We encourage our peers to follow suit."

The move escalates a policy Tidal introduced nearly five months ago, which demonetized AI-powered songs, required artists to label tracks as AI-generated or AI-assisted, and banned AI material tied to fraudulent activity, including impersonations of established artists.

Competitors have so far stopped short of outright bans. Apple Music has said it will label AI-generated and AI-assisted tracks, while Spotify has introduced an "AI Persona" tag for artists it identifies as AI creations. In a blog post last month, Spotify said it had pulled 50 million spam tracks from user recommendations this year after removing 75 million from its catalog entirely, writing that "this work isn't finished."

items.title: U2 Announces North American Leg of ‘Greatest Show on Earth’ Global Stadium Tour for 2027
items.summary:
U2 has added 15 North American stadium dates to Carnaval De Luz Presents: The Greatest Show on Earth World Tour 2027, covering the United States and Canada between August and October of that year. Stephen Wilson Jr. opens the first run of shows, with the War on Drugs taking over support duties for the later dates.

The leg begins August 13 at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami, then moves through Atlanta's Mercedes-Benz Stadium, Baltimore's M&T Bank Stadium, two nights at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, Chicago's Soldier Field, two Toronto shows and Gillette Stadium in Foxborough. The War on Drugs joins beginning September 27 at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, followed by two nights at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles, Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara and a close at Vancouver's BC Place on October 18.

The North American announcement fills in the back half of a tour that U2 had already mapped across Latin America, the UK and Europe. The run opens February 23 at Estadio GNP Seguros in Mexico City and winds through São Paulo, Buenos Aires, Stockholm, Paris, Barcelona, Seville, Lisbon, Amsterdam, London and Berlin before the European portion ends July 9 at Milan's Stadio San Siro.

Demand for those earlier dates has been heavy. Nearly every announced show in Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, the Netherlands, the UK and Germany is already sold out, with only scattered tickets left in Stockholm, Barcelona, Seville and Milan.

Variety reported the ticketing schedule for the new dates: a U2.com subscriber presale opens November 30 at 10 a.m., a Visa cardholder presale runs December 2 from 10 a.m. to 10 p.m., and an artist presale follows December 3 at 10 a.m. General onsale begins December 4 at 10 a.m. through U2.com.
